sermon.title: Four Difficult Issues to Understand Part 2
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: In this second part of the series Pastor David G. Kincer teaches that the death, burial and resurrection of Jesus destroyed the Devil’s power, and that a born-again believer’s new nature is not to sin. He says Satan is still released and bound to influence the world, but is limited by God, using Paul’s thorn in the flesh, pride, marriage and sexual relationships as examples. He closes by saying we do not have to wait for the rapture to experience God’s power.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added by hand, and obvious caption errors were corrected; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor notes: the captions give “2 Chronicles 12:7” and “2 Chron— uh, Corinthians 4:3”; the passages he reads are 2 Corinthians 12:7 and 2 Corinthians 4:3, which are shown. The reference “Acts 26:18” and the other verse quotations use King James wording at points, where the NKJV differs slightly; his words are unchanged. He gives views on sexuality, marriage and other denominations; these are his words and are not verified by this site. “[Unclear]” marks two spots: about 0:50 and about 16:00.

faqs.question: According to this sermon, what happened to the Devil at the cross?
faqs.answer: He says “through the cross the Devil was destroyed, his power was reduced to zero.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: Inasmuch then as the children have partaken of flesh and blood, He Himself likewise shared in the same, that through death He might destroy him who had the power of death, that is, the devil,

faqs.question: What does he say the works of the Devil are?
faqs.answer: He says “what’s the works of the Devil? Him getting you to sin.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: He who sins is of the devil, for the devil has sinned from the beginning. For this purpose the Son of God was manifested, that He might destroy the works of the devil. Whoever has been born of God does not sin, for His seed remains in him; and he cannot sin, because he has been born of God.

faqs.question: Does he say being born again is just saying a sinner’s prayer?
faqs.answer: No. He says “it’s not just repeating a sinner’s prayer, it’s not just getting on a church roll book.”

faqs.question: What does he say about quarreling between denominations?
faqs.answer: He says “we need to quit quarreling with one another and just serve the same Jesus.”

faqs.question: How does he say a Christian overcomes the wicked one?
faqs.answer: He says “how did they do it? By the word of God,” and that you speak the word to yourself instead of using “people’s opinion and your feelings and your circumstances.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: I have written to you, fathers, Because you have known Him who is from the beginning. I have written to you, young men, Because you are strong, and the word of God abides in you, And you have overcome the wicked one.

faqs.question: What does he say young Christians should read?
faqs.answer: He says they “need to be reading Proverbs and singing Psalms and studying the New Testament all the time.”

faqs.question: Does he say Satan can take total control of a believer’s life?
faqs.answer: No. He says God is “not going to let Satan come and just totally have possession of your life,” and that Satan is “totally limited.”

faqs.question: Why does he say there is a price to pay for giving in to sin?
faqs.answer: He says “he wants you to turn, and if there’s no price to pay, you won’t turn.”

faqs.question: Who does he say blinds the minds of unbelievers?
faqs.answer: He reads 2 Corinthians 4:3 and says Satan has that kind of influence: “once you’re blind and the light comes… the whole body is full of light.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: But even if our gospel is veiled, it is veiled to those who are perishing, whose minds the god of this age has blinded, who do not believe, lest the light of the gospel of the glory of Christ, who is the image of God, should shine on them.

faqs.question: What does he say the thorn in the flesh was?
faqs.answer: He says it “wasn’t a physical thing,” but “an angel that opposed him so he didn’t get lifted up with pride.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: And lest I should be exalted above measure by the abundance of the revelations, a thorn in the flesh was given to me, a messenger of Satan to buffet me, lest I be exalted above measure.

faqs.question: Does he say a lack of self-control opens a door to Satan?
faqs.answer: Yes. He says Satan “will take advantage of us for our lack of what? Self-control” and “you’re opening the door for Satan to come in and tempt you.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: Do not deprive one another except with consent for a time, that you may give yourselves to fasting and prayer; and come together again so that Satan does not tempt you because of your lack of self-control.

faqs.question: How does he say Satan keeps people from Bible study?
faqs.answer: He says Satan “wants you to think you’re stupid and can’t understand,” and “loves you saying, ‘man, I just don’t get this book.’”

faqs.question: What does he say about couples living together outside marriage?
faqs.answer: He asks how many Christians “are shacking up,” and says “they’re using grace and faith to justify it.” He says clear Bible direction, when not followed, lets Satan entice us to sin.
